changes: Replaced the upright conical envelope with selected rounded swept whorls, an oblique axis, a reflected adult lip and closed protoconch exterior. Internal shell architecture and apposition remain approximate.
Joined the head, foot and mantle exterior into one connected closed skin mesh and seated its shoulder nearer the aperture. Removed the visible old neck/foot primitive seam.
Added original irregular pigment and granular skin artwork, four fleshy tapered tentacles and retained terminal eye cues. All texture pixels come from reproducible numerical functions.
Baked three reusable maps to remove repeated per-mesh numerical texture generation; the viewer waits for those maps before marking the specimen ready.

Added study-time pause and attributed PNG capture to the archive. Captured images identify a rendered authored view, disclose illustrative scale/time, and retain available artist/source/license credit.
Retained the same surfaces during the existing finite glide; no unfinished biological mechanism was relabelled available.

before: Upright conical external envelope rather than rounded coiled volumes and oblique carriage.
Separate head/neck/foot primitives and a conspicuous tissue seam.
Smooth putty-like skin, weak broken pigment and thin sensory stalks.
Rigid body translation does not reproduce adhesive crawling.
after: Continuous rounded sweep and more plausible selected adult carriage; apical end closed.
Single connected external skin surface, including supported sole and mantle transition.
Source-guided original shell/skin appearance and thicker stalks, still partly stylized.
Glide remains partial and uncalibrated; pedal mechanics are still unfinished.

limitations: This is an unmeasured authored adult reconstruction, not a scan, photorealism certification or independently validated anatomy. Whorl apposition, columella/umbilical closure, shell thickness, aperture/mantle folds, pneumostome, proportions, tissue relief and optical response remain approximate or incomplete. The selected 4.75 turns and 45-degree axis are authored choices within qualitative source comparison, not specimen measurements. Skin/pigment still have numerical regularity and incomplete natural variation, wear and secretions. The existing five-second glide is unchanged: local stalk articulation and bounded body translation, without pedal-wave kinematics, stationary-interwave contact, mucus/traction, feeding or retraction. Default WebGL skin projection is richer than compatibility/GLB UV sampling. No accuracy percentage, expert credential, independent review or physiological simulation is claimed.

anatomy.name: Shell
anatomy.description: Selected 4.75-turn dextral shell sweep with an oblique display axis and reflected adult lip. Whorl volumes, apposition, aperture and carriage are qualitative selections, not measured specimen coordinates; internal shell architecture is incomplete.

anatomy.name: Upper tentacles
anatomy.description: Two longer fleshy sensory stalks with terminal eye cues and two shorter lower tentacles. Small bounded bends retain the same stalks and eyes. Optical organs, neural activity and full retraction are not simulated.

anatomy.name: Foot
anatomy.description: Single joined external head-foot-mantle skin surface with a supported sole and original granular relief cues. The bounded glide has no implemented pedal wave, mucus rheology, traction or calibrated locomotion. Mantle tissues and pneumostome remain incomplete.

privateHistory: Earlier private candidates were rejected for detached/upward shells, missing head closure, flat mesh normals and large polygonal skin cells. Initial topology checks then found collapsed faces and a clipped posterior field boundary; the faces and field bounds were corrected without dropping the closed-surface gate. A direct-download event wait in development timed out; capture now presents the actual PNG with attribution and a download link. Detailed page/figure retrieval for Lai2010 timed out after introductory PDF text was readable; no figure/video/trajectory fit is claimed.
